bbva.resumen: Methodological discrepancy in the baseline due to scope expansion
bbva.descripcion: The base-year 2023 absolute-emissions figure has been restated, changing from 3.2 MtCO2e in the 2024 report to 3.8 MtCO2e in the 2025 one due to the inclusion of 'midstream' activities, which has a detrimental impact on comparability as no proportional readjustment of the final target percentage was disclosed.

bbva.resumen: Baseline scenario update and improved ambition
bbva.descripcion: Emissions intensity fell sharply from 145 kgCO2e/MWh reported in 2024 to 122 kgCO2e/MWh in 2025, a positive change driven by the adoption of the International Energy Agency's updated NZE 2023 scenario, which strengthens the pathway to 2030.

bbva.resumen: Sharp, unjustified increase in emissions intensity
bbva.descripcion: An atypical spike is identified in the portfolio's physical intensity, rising from 1.25 tCO2e/t of steel in the 2024 report to 1.40 tCO2e/t in the 2025 report, moving the bank severely away from its reduction pathway without any explicit justification for this deviation.
The physical intensity metric (gCO2/km) evolves normally along the expected pathway, showing no sharp variations or scope changes between 2024 and 2025 that are significant for the analysis.

The portfolio's evolution confirms a stable decarbonization pathway aligned with the current target, with no methodological changes, sharp increases or quantitative inconsistencies between the 2024 and 2025 publications.

bbva.resumen: Addition of commitments for the air-cargo segment
bbva.descripcion: Whereas the 2024 report's measurement was limited exclusively to commercial passenger airlines, the 2025 report strengthens the scope by officially integrating cargo transport and consolidating a new joint reduction target of 18% for 2030.

bbva.resumen: Transition to the Poseidon Principles v4
bbva.descripcion: The measurement methodology changes drastically, abandoning the standard AER indicator from the 2024 report to adopt in 2025 the new Poseidon Principles v4 alignment trajectory, which makes a direct comparison of the shipping portfolio's scores between the two reporting cycles impossible.
The institution does not report decarbonization targets, reference scenarios or intensity metrics for this commercial real estate sector in either of the two annual reports analyzed.
The institution does not report decarbonization targets, reference scenarios or intensity metrics for this residential mortgage sector in either of the two annual reports analyzed.

The bank increases its climate ambition by bringing forward its commitment to fully eliminate its thermal-coal exposure globally, moving from the 2040 target set in the 2024 report to a new deadline set at 2038 in the 2025 report.

bbva.resumen: First target set for the sector
bbva.descripcion: The sector is added as a new metric in the 2025 report, setting a foundational intensity-reduction target of 25% for 2030, and therefore lacks a quantitative comparison as it was not included in the 2024 report's scope.
The institution does not report decarbonization targets, reference scenarios or intensity metrics for the primary-sector portfolio in either of the two annual reports analyzed.

santander.resumen: Santander changed its target in the oil and gas sector from an absolute-emissions cap to an intensity metric
santander.descripcion: The target changes from a single absolute-emissions value (16.98 MtCO2e in the 2024 report) to an intensity range of 2.31–3.03 tCO2e/TJ in the 2025 report.

santander.resumen: Exclusion of Scope 3 emissions from the alignment target, lowering climate stringency by ignoring the impact of fossil-fuel end use.
santander.descripcion:
The alignment target in the 2025 report now focuses exclusively on Scopes 1 and 2, whereas the 2024 report included Scopes 1, 2 and 3 in its absolute-reduction target.
The bank argues that clients have greater operational control over Scopes 1 and 2, and that Scope 3 emissions are now monitored through the new "Primary Energy Index" due to their strong dependence on global demand.

santander.resumen: Methodological update of the base year to 2023
santander.descripcion: The base year is reported to have been updated to 2023 in the 2025 report, replacing the 2019 base year used in the 2024 report.

santander.resumen: Metric change towards a target range that reflects the different regional and regulatory transition speeds, replacing the single fixed-value target for 2030
santander.descripcion: The 2030 target has moved from a fixed value of 0.11 tCO2e/MWh to a target range of 102–124 kgCO2e/MWh to reflect the different regional and regulatory transition speeds, also changing the unit to kg instead of tonnes (t).

santander.resumen: Strong improvement in the portfolio's physical performance with a significant drop in physical emissions intensity, driven mainly by reduced exposure to intensive clients and the financing of renewable projects
santander.descripcion: Physical emissions intensity fell significantly from 0.15 tCO2e/MWh in 2023 to 88 kgCO2e/MWh (0.088 tCO2e/MWh) in 2024, driven by reduced exposure to carbon-intensive clients and increased financing of renewable projects still under construction.

santander.resumen: Accounting discrepancy in the reported 2023 exposure data
santander.descripcion: A discrepancy is observed in the exposure figures (drawn balance in billions of euros) for financial year 2023 between the published reports: the 2024 report states EUR 10.75 billion, while the 2025 report states EUR 12.79 billion for the same period. Santander provides no justification for the change.

santander.resumen: Relaxation of the 2030 target, moving from a fixed target to a more permissive range, granting more room to finance less efficient steel operations.
santander.descripcion: The 2030 target is reported to have been updated in the 2025 report to a range of 1.17–1.28, replacing the single value of 1.07 recorded in the 2024 report.

santander.resumen: Methodological update shifting the reference base year for portfolio measurement to 2023.
santander.descripcion: The base year has been updated to 2023 for the 2025 report, replacing the 2019 base year used in the 2024 report.

santander.resumen: Notable year-on-year increase in physical emissions intensity, justified by the bank as a change in portfolio composition caused by the run-off of low-emission clients
santander.descripcion: Intensity rose from the 1.38 tCO2e/tS reported for 2023 (2024 report, p. 48) to 1.51 tCO2e/tS for 2024 (2025 report, p. 61) due to a change in portfolio composition from the run-off of low-emission client profiles.

santander.resumen: Shift to ranges for the manufacturing and lending portfolios
santander.descripcion: The 2030 targets have been loosened, moving from fixed targets of 103 gCO2/vkm in manufacturing and 75–89 gCO2e/vkm in European lending to ranges of 80–98 gCO2/vkm and 70–109 gCO2e/vkm respectively, thus reflecting the different regional transition scenarios and the volatility of the electric-car market.

santander.resumen: Easing of transition stringency by adopting a mixed scenario (NZE2050 + APS)
santander.descripcion: The bank has replaced the IEA Net Zero 2050 scenario for both subsectors with the combined IEA NZE2050 and APS scenarios.

santander.resumen: The sector has no active reporting of metrics, targets or exposure in either of the two years analyzed.
Withdrawal of the formal 2030 reduction target due to technological and market barriers, downgrading the exposure to a mere "monitoring" portfolio.
santander.descripcion: Sector reclassification (removed as a target) — The aviation sector has moved from having a defined 2030 alignment target of 61.71 gCO2e/RPK to being classified solely as a monitoring portfolio with no set target, a decision justified by its lower alignment materiality and its strong dependence on external factors such as sustainable fuels (SAF) and slow technological progress.

santander.resumen: The sector has no active reporting of metrics, targets or exposure in either of the two years analyzed.
Expansion of the climate-risk consolidation scope by integrating the commercial-property and mortgage data of the Portugal subsidiary.
santander.descripcion: The financed-emissions analysis of the commercial real estate sector has been expanded by adding the Portugal portfolio to the Spain and UK metrics reported the previous year (2024 report, p. 49; 2025 report, p. 61).

The exposure reported at year-end 2024 is EUR 4.2 billion in the 2025 report, whereas for the same 2024 year-end the 2024 report stated EUR 4.8 billion.
The 2025 exposure value is added, standing at EUR 2.3 billion.

santander.resumen: The sector has no active reporting of metrics, targets or exposure in either of the two years analyzed.
Refinement in the measurement of the Brazil portfolio, narrowing the risk analysis to the most material subsectors: soy, maize and beef cattle.
santander.descripcion: The measurement of financed emissions in Brazil's agricultural portfolio has been refined to specifically include only soy, maize and beef cattle, which has meant recalculating the base emissions reported in 2023 from 9.83 MtCO2e to 8.41 MtCO2e to ensure comparability.

sabadell.resumen: Absolute emissions rose to 5,277 Kt CO2e due to new credit drawdowns, although they remain within the established limits.
sabadell.descripcion: Absolute emissions spiked to 5,277 Kt CO2e, breaking the previous year's downward trend (4,820 Kt CO2e), an increase the bank attributes to new credit drawdowns in sector companies, though it stresses that they remain below the limit pathway.

sabadell.resumen: Carbon intensity fell to 40 Kg CO2e/MWh, beating the 2030 target thanks to the push in renewables and improvements in the corporate portfolio.
sabadell.descripcion: Physical intensity fell sharply to 40 Kg CO2e/MWh, dropping below the 45–85 target range set for 2030 — an acceleration the bank explains by the strong contribution of renewable-energy project finance, the improvement in corporate clients' intensity and the natural maturities/repayments of the portfolio, versus the 63 Kg CO2e/MWh reported the previous year.

sabadell.resumen: No relevant changes were reported in the period.
Physical intensity fell from 220 to 183 gCO2e/vkm due to greater credit exposure to companies aligned with the 2030 decarbonization targets.
sabadell.descripcion: Physical intensity recorded a pronounced fall, moving from 220 gCO2e/vkm to 183 gCO2e/vkm, a substantial improvement the institution attributes to the rise in credit exposure to corporate groups whose intensities are already aligned with the 2030 decarbonization pathway.

sabadell.resumen: No relevant changes were reported in the indicated period.
No relevant changes were recorded in the reported period.
Physical intensity rose 9.8% due to changes in the client-portfolio composition, exceeding base-year levels.
sabadell.descripcion: Physical intensity underwent an atypical 9.8% increase, rising to 708 Kg CO2e/tn versus 645 Kg CO2e/tn in the base year, a deviation the bank attributes to changes in the composition of a highly concentrated client portfolio; it is a monitoring metric that was not detailed in the previous report.

sabadell.resumen: The Alignment Delta metric rose to +28% due to a time lag from using 2023 vessel data for the 2024 estimates.
sabadell.descripcion: The Alignment Delta metric worsened, rising to +28% compared with the +25% of the base year, an upward deviation the bank explains by a time lag in the data: as it did not have updated vessel figures for 2024, it had to use 2023 vessel data to estimate the 2024 delta.

sabadell.resumen: Drawn risk increased to EUR 1.7 million due to variations in a factoring line maturing before 2030.
sabadell.descripcion: Drawn risk spiked to EUR 1.7 million, in sharp contrast with the reduction to EUR 0.1 million the previous year, attributed to fluctuations in the drawdown of a factoring line maturing before 2030.

sabadell.resumen: No material variations are identified in the information analyzed.

caixabank.descripcion: Although the 2030 reduction target remains unchanged, the 2025 report consolidates a drop in absolute emissions to 4.9 MtCO2e versus the 5.6 MtCO2e previously published in 2024, comfortably beating the final 6.99 MtCO2e milestone ahead of schedule due to the volatility of drawn exposure.

caixabank.resumen: Discrepancy in a historical figure and early achievement of the target
caixabank.descripcion: A methodological alteration is evident, changing the 2022 figure from 116 kgCO2e/MWh (2024 report) to 118 kgCO2e/MWh (2025 report), while a strong improvement is reported as it fell in 2025 to 79 kgCO2e/MWh, thus beating the final target of 95 kgCO2e/MWh set for 2030.

The sector keeps its reduction target of between 10% and 20% for 2030 in both reports, reflecting a favourable evolution of the metric towards 991 kgCO2e/t in 2025 with no discrepancies detected in the previously reported historical values.

caixabank.resumen: Reporting discrepancy and severe setback in the metric
caixabank.descripcion: The 2025 document retroactively changes the 2023 figure to 148 gCO2/vkm, in contrast with the 146 gCO2/vkm stated in 2024, and reports a serious worsening in 2025 as it climbs to 163.9 gCO2/vkm, exceeding even its base year due to the impact of the loosening of European automotive-sector targets.

Both reports identically confirm the decision not to set decarbonization targets for this portfolio due to its low materiality, keeping it under a strict monitoring plan with no significant methodological or numerical changes.

The 30% reduction target for 2030 and the scope over airlines are maintained in both years, evidencing a favourable and consistent decarbonization pathway with no anomalous numerical changes or alterations to its base year.

The characteristics of the 0% convergence target for 2030 of the Alignment Delta metric remain unchanged between the 2024 and 2025 reports, following the publication timelines of the Poseidon Principles with no inconsistencies noted.

caixabank.resumen: Worsening of the metric due to a proxy-data update
caixabank.descripcion: Even though the 2030 target remains intact, the 2025 report shows an intensity increase to 21 kgCO2e/m2 versus the 20.1 kgCO2e/m2 shown in 2024, exceeding its base year because of an update to the proxies used that negatively affects performance.

The metric approach and the 19% reduction target are consolidated in both reports with no discrepancies, reflecting a stabilization in 2025 after the decrease previously achieved thanks to the integration of actual energy-efficiency certificates.

The unmovable target of a full phase-out of thermal-coal financing by 2030 is confirmed, and although slight operational variations in exposure are seen, there are no methodological or strategic changes versus 2024.

caixabank.resumen: No significant changes; the Aluminium sector has no climate target set
caixabank.descripcion: The most recent report ratifies the strategy set out in 2024 of postponing the setting of a climate target because its exposure does not reach the 1% materiality threshold, continuing with the monthly monitoring model unchanged.

caixabank.resumen: No significant changes; the Agriculture sector has no quantitative climate target set
caixabank.descripcion: In both corporate documents the institution refrains from establishing a quantitative metric due to a lack of methodological maturity, opting to keep its qualitative goal unchanged, focused on increasing sector knowledge and dialogue.

hsbc.resumen: HSBC adjusted its 2030 emission-reduction targets and updated the 2019 baseline.
hsbc.descripcion:
The absolute emissions-reduction target for 2030 has moved from a fixed -34% target to a target range of -14% to -30%, now based on the IEA's APS and NZE 2024 scenarios replacing NZE 2021. The baseline value (2019) has been recalculated from 42.6 Mt CO2e to 46.2 Mt CO2e, an 8% increase due to the inclusion of short-term lending and improved identification of project financing.
Reported financed emissions moved from 23.2 Mt CO2e in the 2024 annual report to 28.9 Mt CO2e in the 2025 annual report, for the year 2023.

hsbc.resumen: The bank updated its base year to 2023, renewed its climate scenarios and integrated sustainable financing, adjusting its 2030 emissions-intensity targets.
hsbc.descripcion:
The bank has updated the base year from 2019, with an intensity of 513.4 tCO2e/GWh, to 2023 with 295 tCO2e/GWh, to reflect improvements in data availability and methodologies.
The bank has replaced the IEA NZE 2021 scenario with the IEA NZE and APS 2024 scenarios.
The bank has incorporated consideration of "use of proceeds" financing and financing for purely "green" clients, which has driven recalculations in this sector.
The 2030 intensity target changed from a fixed target of 138 tCO2e/GWh to a range of 195–270 tCO2e/GWh.

hsbc.resumen: The aluminium sector was split out from the group, the reference year was updated to 2023, and the 2030 emissions-intensity targets were adjusted.
hsbc.descripcion: The aluminium sector has been split out from the group, moving from "Iron, steel and aluminium" exclusively to "Iron and steel" due to its low materiality. The reference year moved from 2019 to 2023, with an adjusted baseline of 1.73 tCO2e/t steel. The 2030 intensity target changed from 1.05 tCO2e/t metal to a range of 1.29–1.52 tCO2e/t steel.

hsbc.resumen: The base year was updated to 2023 and the 2030 intensity target was adjusted, replacing the fixed target with a range of values.
hsbc.descripcion: The base year was updated from 2019 to 2023 with a value of 152.8 tCO2e/mn vkm. The 2030 intensity target moved from a fixed target of 66 tCO2e/mn vkm to a range of 65.5–95.3 tCO2e/mn vkm.

hsbc.resumen: Transition to a less demanding target range and a change of base year.
hsbc.descripcion: The single-value target of 0.46 tCO2e/t of cement was turned into a range of 0.47–0.56 tCO2e/t for 2030, setting 2023 as the new base year at 0.59 tCO2e/t and recording a slight intensity increase in 2024 to 0.61 tCO2e/t.

hsbc.resumen: The aluminium sector has been removed from the alignment-target framework due to its low representativeness on the balance sheet.
hsbc.descripcion: The aluminium sector has been removed from the alignment-target framework due to its limited weight on the balance sheet. It previously formed part of the "Iron, steel and aluminium" group.

hsbc.resumen: The 2020 base year was recalculated to 3.4 Mt CO2e, and a 94% reduction in financed emissions was recorded by 2024 due to lower lending activity.
hsbc.descripcion:
The reference emissions value for base year 2020 has been recalculated from 4.7 Mt CO2e to 3.4 Mt CO2e due to a refinement of scope and the exclusions framework.
Financed emissions fell drastically from 1.44 Mt CO2e at year-end 2022 to 0.22 Mt CO2e in 2024, an 94% drop versus the new base year due to lower financing of specific projects and low levels of loan drawdown.

hsbc.resumen: The requested information is not available in the current records.
The information is not available in the reports consulted.
The information is not available in the reports consulted.

barclays.resumen: The absolute-emissions reduction worsened from -45% to -41% due to higher client credit drawdowns and enterprise-value volatility.
barclays.descripcion: The cumulative absolute-emissions reduction versus the base year has worsened, moving from -45% at 41.1 MtCO2e to -41% at 43.7 MtCO2e, an increase attributed to higher use of credit lines by clients and the volatility of enterprise value (EVIC) in the calculation.

barclays.resumen: The bank unified its methodology under the IEA NZE 2050 scenario and updated the base-year physical intensity from 311 to 316 kgCO2e/MWh.
barclays.descripcion: The bank has removed the previously used IEA SDS scenario, keeping only the IEA NZE 2050 scenario for this sector. The base-year (2020) physical intensity has been recalculated from 311 kgCO2e/MWh to 316 kgCO2e/MWh.

barclays.resumen: No relevant changes are reported in the content analyzed.
No relevant changes are reported in the content analyzed.
The sector's financed emissions rose from 0.8 to 1.5 MtCO2e due to the addition of a new client and the small portfolio's high sensitivity to credit variations.
barclays.descripcion: The sector's absolute financed emissions have almost doubled, rising from 0.8 MtCO2e to 1.5 MtCO2e, due to the addition of a new client and the disproportionate impact any credit variation has on a portfolio made up of very few clients.

barclays.resumen: No relevant variations are recorded in the content.
Indicates that no relevant changes have occurred in the corresponding period or category.
No relevant changes are reported in the information provided.
A downward adjustment has been made to the base-year (2023) physical emissions intensity.
barclays.descripcion: The base-year (2023) physical intensity has been recalculated downwards, moving from 30.0 kgCO2e/m2 to 26.3 kgCO2e/m2.

barclays.resumen: The base-year (2023) physical intensity for the UK mortgage portfolio was reduced due to improved data quality and a methodological review.
barclays.descripcion: The base-year (2023) physical intensity for the UK mortgage portfolio has been reduced following a methodological review, from 32.1 kgCO2e/m2 to 27.9 kgCO2e/m2, due to improved data quality.

barclays.resumen: The requested information is not available in the current records.
No significant changes are presented in the document analyzed.

natwest.resumen: The base year and the 2030 target have been readjusted
natwest.descripcion:
Substantial changes have been introduced to the oil and gas sector's climate management. First, a new 2030 target has been set: a 13% reduction in the physical emissions intensity of production-financing activities. This change comes together with a metric update, setting 2023 as the new base year at 69.8 tCO₂e/TJ (versus the 2024 report, which set the base at 2019 at 4.1 tCO₂e/TJ with a 76% reduction target).

Structurally, this sector's positions have been grouped together with power generation and coal under the "E&S Energy Supply Sectors RAC" framework. Likewise, the reporting scope for Scope 3 financed emissions has been broadened, moving from covering only upstream clients to covering the entire sector. Lastly, a new mandatory oversight forum has been created for all financing above £50 million, focused on closely assessing ESG ratings and clients' transition planning.

natwest.resumen: The reporting methodology moved towards portfolio-level activity-based targets, integrating the power sector into the new E&S Energy Supply Sectors RAC framework.
natwest.descripcion: The reporting methodology has evolved from sector-only targets to "portfolio-level activity-based targets," with the report noting that the current charts should not be directly compared with the previous year's. The sector has been integrated into the new "E&S Energy Supply Sectors RAC" framework.

natwest.resumen: NatWest withdrew its SBTi-validated climate targets for iron and steel in favour of its own methodological framework.
natwest.descripcion: NatWest had SBTi-validated targets for iron and steel with emissions of 0.1 MtCO2e, which have disappeared in the 2025 target update. The bank has withdrawn its SBTi-validated targets, opting for a framework of its own design not validated by that initiative.

natwest.resumen: Road transport was reclassified under the Mobility pillar, and manufacturing emissions intensity fell in 2024.
natwest.descripcion: Road transport has been reclassified under the strategic "Mobility" pillar, with a renewed focus on supporting the electrification of clients' fleets. Manufacturing emissions intensity fell from 230.5 gCO2e/v-km in 2023 to 185.9 gCO2e/v-km in 2024.

natwest.resumen: The bank excluded the cement sector, previously SBTi-validated, from its new activity-based target framework.
natwest.descripcion: The bank reported SBTi-validated targets for cement with emissions of 0.03 MtCO2e, but this sector was excluded from the new activity-based target framework.

natwest.resumen: The bank set a new 19% reduction target for 2030 in the aviation sector, based on a 2023 baseline.
natwest.descripcion: The bank had no aviation targets in 2024 and added a 19% reduction target for 2030 with a 2023 baseline for aircraft operators and lessors. The reported physical intensity is 907.6 tCO2e/Mn RTK.

natwest.resumen: The bank removed the sector from its activity-based target reporting and folded the aluminium target into the hard-to-abate industries dashboard.
natwest.descripcion: The bank reported emissions of 0.002 MtCO2e with SBTi-validated targets, but the sector has been removed from activity-based target reporting. The aluminium target has been folded into the "Hard-to-Abate Industries" dashboard, whereas it was previously reported as an independent monitoring metric.

natwest.resumen: The bank implemented Annual Efficiency Ratio reporting for vessels and adhered to the IMO's decarbonization pathway with a 2030 alignment target.
natwest.descripcion: Reporting of the "Annual Efficiency Ratio" (AER) metric has been introduced for the first time for the vessel-financing portfolio, replacing the previous year's qualitative monitoring. The bank has formalized its adherence to the International Maritime Organization's (IMO) strengthened 2023 decarbonization pathway, setting a portfolio alignment target for 2030.

natwest.resumen: CRE portfolio coverage was expanded to logistics and warehousing, achieving a reduction in emissions intensity to 29 kgCO2e/m2 and adding energy-certification targets.
natwest.descripcion:
CRE portfolio coverage has been expanded to include logistics and warehousing assets, increasing the total volume of measured assets by 12%. Emissions intensity moved from 32 kgCO2e/m2 to 29 kgCO2e/m2 due to grid improvements and a shift towards more efficient buildings.
The target has evolved from a measurement based solely on operational carbon intensity to a dual target that includes the percentage of assets with A-to-C energy performance certificates (EPC).

natwest.resumen: The bank updated its 2030 emissions-reduction target and recorded an increase in the proportion of mortgages with efficient energy certification.
natwest.descripcion: The bank replaced its 49% reduction target for 2030 with a 2019 baseline with a 26% target for 2030 with a 2023 baseline. The percentage of mortgages with EPC C or above rose from 46.3% to 48.8% in 2025.

natwest.resumen: The exit from UK coal clients was completed in October 2024, keeping the global exit target for 2030
natwest.descripcion: The commitment to exit clients with coal production in the UK, related infrastructure and thermal generation has been completed with a deadline of 1 October 2024, while keeping the total global exit target for 2030.

natwest.resumen: The agriculture sector now prioritizes decarbonization potential, setting a 9% reduction target for 2030 with a 2023 baseline.
natwest.descripcion:
The approach to agriculture has moved from a general emissions measurement to a prioritization of "decarbonization potential and impact."
The 2030 reduction target has been set at 9% with a 2023 baseline, removing the previous 26% target with a 2019 baseline.

stanchart.resumen: The 2025 report changes the upstream Scope 3 emissions methodology, restates the 2024 figure, and reports 7.2 MtCO2e for 2025.
stanchart.descripcion: The 2025 report reveals a change in the proxy approach used to determine the sector's emissions; it now only counts Scope 3 emissions from upstream production activities (including diversified and integrated counterparties), based on improvements in data quality. Due to the methodological change, the 2025 report restates the 2024 absolute financed-emissions figure, moving from 9.4 MtCO2e to 8.76 MtCO2e.

stanchart.resumen: Power-sector emissions intensity fell from 0.43 to 0.39 tCO2/MWh between 2024 and 2025 due to lower coal exposure and increased renewable-energy financing.
stanchart.descripcion:
Intensity fell from 0.43 tCO2/MWh in the 2024 report to 0.39 tCO2/MWh in the 2025 report.
The bank attributes this improvement to reduced exposure to thermal-coal power generation as balances mature, and to increased financing of renewable-energy and lower-intensity gas projects.

stanchart.resumen: Emissions intensity fell from 1.87 to 1.75 tCO2/t due to a higher proportion of clients using electric-arc furnaces with scrap.
stanchart.descripcion: The 2024 report reported 1.87 tCO2/t (2023 data). The 2025 report reports 1.75 tCO2/t (2024 data). This is due to a greater portfolio weight of clients using scrap (electric-arc furnaces) versus those using iron ore in blast furnaces.

stanchart.resumen: Reported emissions fell from 157 gCO2/Vkm in the 2024 report to 145 gCO2/Vkm in the 2025 report.
stanchart.descripcion: The 2024 report reported 157 gCO2/Vkm (2023 data). The 2025 report reports 145 gCO2/Vkm (2024 data).

stanchart.resumen: The 2025 report projects a short-term slowdown in the decarbonization pathway due to looser environmental policies and the continued relevance of combustion engines.
stanchart.descripcion: The 2025 report notes "headwinds" from the loosening of decarbonization policies and manufacturers' acknowledgment that internal-combustion-engine production will remain significant, which could flatten the short-term decarbonization pathway.

stanchart.resumen: Emissions intensity fell from 0.62 to 0.60 tCO2/t due to energy optimization at financed clients' plants and increased use of clinker substitutes.
stanchart.descripcion: The 2024 report reported 0.62 tCO2/t (2023 data). The 2025 report reports a decrease to 0.60 tCO2/t (2024 data). This is due to increased lending to clients with lower production intensities thanks to improved energy efficiency at their plants and greater use of clinker substitutes.

stanchart.resumen: Emissions intensity fell to 771 gCO2e/RTK in 2025, moving below the 2030 target.
stanchart.descripcion: Intensity fell from 782 gCO2e/RTK in the 2024 report to 771 gCO2e/RTK in the 2025 report, moving below the 2030 target (773).

stanchart.resumen: The 2025 report presents, for the first time, the breakdown of Scope 1, 2 and 3 emissions for the sector.
stanchart.descripcion: The 2025 report breaks down, for the first time, the sector's Scope 1 and 2 (1.0 MtCO2e) and Scope 3 (0.2 MtCO2e) emissions.

stanchart.resumen: The alignment delta showed a substantial improvement, moving from +3.2% in 2024 to -0.9% in 2025.
stanchart.descripcion: The alignment delta improved significantly, moving from the +3.2% reported in the 2024 report to -0.9% in the 2025 report. This places the metric very close to the zero-value target set for 2030.

stanchart.resumen: The 2025 report details, for the first time, the shipping sector's Scope 1, 2 and 3 emissions, totalling 3.0 MtCO2e.
stanchart.descripcion: The 2025 report breaks down and reports, for the first time, Scope 1, 2 and 3 emissions for the shipping sector (Scope 1, 2: 0.5 MtCO2e; Scope 3: 2.5 MtCO2e).

stanchart.resumen: Emissions intensity fell between the 2024 and 2025 reports.
stanchart.descripcion: Intensity fell from 58 kgCO2e/m^2 in the 2024 report to 53 kgCO2e/m^2 in the 2025 report.

stanchart.resumen: The 2025 report reports a portfolio adjustment favouring low-grid-intensity European locations over ASEAN markets.
stanchart.descripcion: The 2025 report mentions a change in the portfolio's location mix, with greater exposure to buildings in European countries (with lower-intensity power grids) and less weight in ASEAN markets with higher intensities.

stanchart.resumen: Emissions fell from 36.0 to 34.2 kgCO2e/m^2 due to grid decarbonization in key Asian markets.
stanchart.descripcion: The 2024 report reported 36.0 kgCO2e/m^2. The 2025 report reports 34.2 kgCO2e/m^2. This reflects the onset of grid decarbonization in Hong Kong, South Korea, Singapore and Taiwan.

stanchart.resumen: A reduction in absolute emissions was recorded, moving from 1.2 MtCO2e in the 2024 report to 1.1 MtCO2e in the 2025 report.
stanchart.descripcion: Absolute emissions fell from 1.2 MtCO2e in the 2024 report to 1.1 MtCO2e in the 2025 report.

stanchart.resumen: A 105% increase in emissions intensity (6.75 tCO2e/t) was recorded due to short-term loans to high-emission aluminium producers.
stanchart.descripcion: The 2024 report reported 3.28 tCO2e/t. The 2025 report reports a drastic 105% increase, reaching 6.75 tCO2e/t. The bank explains that this increase was mainly due to a rise in short-term lending to primary aluminium producers with high emission intensities, maturing in 2025.

stanchart.resumen: The portfolio's ITR was revised upwards due to an update to CDP's scoring methodology.
stanchart.descripcion: The 2025 report revised the portfolio's Implied Temperature Rise (ITR) due to an update to CDP's methodology for default temperature scores, which rose from 3.1°C to 3.4°C.

stanchart.resumen: The 2025 report adjusts the 2023 baseline to 2.96°C and raises the 2030 target range to 2.4–2.6°C following the CDP revision.
stanchart.descripcion: Due to the CDP revision, the 2025 report restates the 2023 baseline from 2.72°C to 2.96°C, and raises the 2030 target range from 2.2–2.4°C (in the 2024 report) to 2.4–2.6°C.

stanchart.resumen: The 2025 report records an ITR of 2.33°C, a 21% decrease compared with the new baseline.
stanchart.descripcion: The 2025 report reports a current ITR of 2.33°C (2024 data), a 21% reduction versus the new baseline.

lloyds.descripcion: The bank maintains its restrictive policy of not approving direct financing for new ("greenfield") oil and gas field developments, originally approved post-2021, with no unforeseen conceptual or numerical changes recorded between the two years.

The power sector remains integrated within the portfolio's overall decarbonization strategy, with no methodological changes or extraordinary quantitative variations explicitly reported between the two periods.
The steel sector is not included within the organization's sectoral financed-emissions decarbonization targets in the corresponding sustainability reports.

lloyds.resumen: Methodological tightening of the target to exclude hybrid vehicles
lloyds.descripcion: The institution strengthened its environmental criteria in the 2025 report by restricting the methodology of its £10 billion motor-financing target for 2027 to cover exclusively pure electric vehicles (EV), unlike the 2024 report, where the previous cumulative £8 billion target jointly included electric and plug-in hybrid vehicles.
The cement sector has no specific sectoral targets or independently reported emissions-intensity metrics from the institution in either of the two years analyzed.

The aviation sector continues to be listed as part of the sectoral commitments made under the Net-Zero Banking Alliance (NZBA), with no detailed changes to its targets or mismatches in its baseline estimation data.
Activities and portfolios associated with international shipping are not the subject of structured numerical or qualitative reporting within the sectoral decarbonization sections analyzed.

lloyds.resumen: Emissions targets updated to the UK's Seventh Carbon Budget
lloyds.descripcion: The bank methodologically reconfigured the sectoral financed-emissions targets for the commercial real estate sector in the 2025 report, adopting the parameters of the Climate Change Committee's (CCC) Seventh Carbon Budget, replacing the Sixth Carbon Budget used as the reference guide in the 2024 report.

lloyds.resumen: Climate recalibration of mortgages and strong growth in cumulative sustainable balances
lloyds.descripcion: The targets for the residential housing portfolio were updated in the 2025 report according to the UK's new Seventh Carbon Budget guidelines versus the Sixth in the 2024 report, reporting an increase in cumulative financing for EPC A- and B-rated energy-efficient properties, which rose from £11.4 billion in the previous document to £18.5 billion in the current period.

lloyds.resumen: Consolidation of the full exit timeline for 2030
lloyds.descripcion: The financial group reinforced the transparency of its decarbonization strategy by projecting a definitive exit from all entities operating thermal-coal plants by 2030 in the 2025 report, complementing the milestone of excluding direct financing for UK thermal-coal power generation achieved at the end of 2023 per the 2024 report.
Aluminium does not appear among the individually assessed industrial categories or portfolios in the financial group's published energy-transition strategies.

lloyds.resumen: Alignment of sectoral targets with the UK's Seventh Carbon Budget
lloyds.descripcion: The financed-emissions target for the agriculture sector was reformulated in the 2025 report to absorb the guidelines of the UK's Seventh Carbon Budget issued by the CCC, breaking from the Sixth Budget framework used as the technical baseline in the 2024 report.

ing.resumen: Shift to loan limits to measure exposure, reflecting a real improvement in intensity and a substantial drop in Mid and Downstream balances.
ing.descripcion: In the Upstream sector, in line with SBTi validation, the institution has adjusted its exposure-measurement methodology, replacing the outstanding-balance criterion (EUR 1,001 million in 2024) with loan limits, which reached EUR 1,900 million in 2025. Likewise, in the Mid and Downstream segments, emissions intensity fell from 19.1 to 19.0 kg CO2e/boe, accompanied by a significant fall in exposure, from EUR 7,400 million to EUR 5,600 million.

ing.resumen: The bank will delay until 2026 the halt to financing new LNG export terminals, aligning with the IEA's warnings about stranded assets.
ing.descripcion: According to the 2025 report, the bank will not finance new LNG export terminals from 2026, a sector that today accounts for 39% of its portfolio's emissions. This represents a delay versus the 2024 report, which pledged to stop this financing in 2025. Despite the delay, the measure supports the IEA's (International Energy Agency) position, which warns of these infrastructures' susceptibility to becoming stranded in a lock-in situation.

ing.resumen: Sharp fall in portfolio emissions intensity driven by strong capital allocation to renewable-project financing.
ing.descripcion: Portfolio emissions intensity has fallen markedly, moving from 63 kg CO2e/MWh in 2024 to 43.6 kg CO2e/MWh in 2025, accompanied by a rise in portfolio volume from EUR 11.5 billion to EUR 13.3 billion, strongly driven by the financing of renewable-energy projects.

ing.resumen: Notable increase in risk appetite for clean energy, raising financial commitments in wind and solar to EUR 9.6 billion.
ing.descripcion: Commitments to wind and solar energy rose from EUR 7.0 billion in the 2024 report to EUR 9.6 billion in the 2025 report.

ing.resumen: Methodological update of the base year for measuring the bank's operational footprint, jumping from 2014 to 2023.
ing.descripcion: The 2025 report sets 2023 as the new base year for the operational footprint, replacing the 2014 reference used in the 2024 report.

ing.resumen: Adoption of the Sustainable Steel Principles (SSP) standard, showing a real improvement in portfolio intensity despite a temporary deviation.
ing.descripcion: The bank has updated the presentation of its alignment metric per the latest Sustainable Steel Principles (SSP) guidance, moving from reporting an "SSP Alignment score" (0.83 in 2024) to a percentage deviation, "SSP percentage deviation" (+5.4% in 2025), achieving despite this temporary deviation a real improvement in the portfolio's emissions intensity, moving from 1.93 to 1.90 t CO2/t steel on an exposure that grew from EUR 2.0 to 2.1 billion.

ing.resumen: Limitation identified in the measurement model, which currently does not capture the positive climate-risk impact of financing "green steel" projects.
ing.descripcion: The 2025 report notes that the current methodology does not yet reflect the impact of financing "green steel" projects under development.

ing.resumen: Slight deterioration in portfolio intensity caused by a composition effect: higher-emitting clients increased their credit-line drawdowns.
ing.descripcion: Emissions intensity rose slightly, from 0.146 kg CO2/vkm in 2024 to 0.150 kg CO2/vkm in 2025 on a stable portfolio volume of EUR 4.0 billion, a dynamic driven by balance increases at specific high-intensity clients that offset average reductions across the rest of the portfolio.

ing.resumen: Worsening of the intensity metric explained by greater use of credit facilities by clients with poorer emissions ratios.
ing.descripcion: Intensity rose slightly, from 0.688 t CO2/t cement in 2024 to 0.695 t CO2/t cement in 2025, while portfolio volume fell from EUR 0.7 to 0.6 billion, as some higher-emission-intensity clients increased their use of credit lines while lower-intensity clients reduced their outstanding exposure.

ing.resumen: Spike in intensity and exposure caused by temporary liquidity distortions, specifically advance payments on lower-emission aircraft.
ing.descripcion: Financial-commitment volume in aviation rose from EUR 4.1 to 4.8 billion between the 2024 and 2025 reports, while emissions intensity rose 2%, from 844 to 861 g CO2e/RTK, attributed in the report to advance payments on lower-emission aircraft facilities that temporarily altered the portfolio's weighting.

ing.resumen: Continued improvement in the 1.5°C alignment pathway, supported by client investment in efficiency and a stricter maritime regulatory environment.
ing.descripcion: The alignment delta versus the 1.5°C scenario has remained in negative (aligned) territory, though moderating from -7.6% in 2024 to -4.6% in 2025, supported by a portfolio volume that held steady at EUR 8.6 billion. The reduction is mainly due to investments made by its clients in energy-efficiency and emissions-reduction technologies. The change is mainly due to variations in the bulk-carrier and tanker segments of its portfolio, which have had a more significant impact on the weighted average intensity this year. Increasingly strict international environmental regulations are also a contributing factor.

ing.resumen: Adoption of the CRREM standard, revealing a significant improvement in the climate intensity of commercial real estate assets amid balance growth.
ing.descripcion: Following an adjustment to emission factors to strictly align with the CRREM model (moving from "Well-to-Wheel" to "Tank-to-Wheel" factors), the 2022 baseline has been adjusted to 37.0 kg CO2e/m2, thus reporting a significant improvement in emissions intensity from 39.5 kg CO2e/m2 in 2024 to 34.0 kg CO2e/m2 in 2025, for an exposure that grew from EUR 26.2 to 27.8 billion.

ing.resumen: Very positive dynamics in the mortgage sector, achieving a reduction in emissions intensity alongside strong growth in financed volume.
ing.descripcion: Mortgage-sector emissions intensity improved versus the previous year, falling from 37.5 kg CO2e/m2 in 2024 to 35.5 kg CO2e/m2 in 2025, alongside strong growth in the portfolio volume under measurement, which rose from EUR 294.3 to 315.0 billion.

ing.resumen: Strict adherence to the coal exit plan, reflected in the continued amortization of direct financing to coal-fired power plants.
ing.descripcion: In line with its coal-exit commitment, financing for individual coal-fired power plants has continued its amortization path, falling from EUR 77 million in 2024 to EUR 63 million in 2025.

ing.resumen: Drastic reduction in the portfolio's transition risk, keeping just one client above the 5% thermal-coal-activity threshold.
ing.descripcion: In 2025 it is identified that only one client remains above the 5% thermal-coal-activity threshold (kept under EU governmental mandate for energy security).

ing.resumen: Expansion of the Terra methodological framework to integrate measurement of the aluminium sector
ing.descripcion: The bank explicitly states that it has begun to incorporate the aluminium sector into the scope of its Terra methodology, so its transition plans are currently under development and no consolidated intensity targets or numerical values are reported.

ing.resumen: Expansion of the climate-risk map to include the dairy sector, for which transition targets are under development.
ing.descripcion: As with aluminium, the bank mentions dairy activity (Dairy, agricultural segment) as a new scope whose transition plans are still under development.

socgen.resumen: Methodological adjustment to the absolute-emissions baseline
socgen.descripcion: Due to a change of data provider and corrections to client data, the 2019 absolute-emissions baseline and the 2030 target have been adjusted (the baseline moved from 29.6 MtCO2eq in the 2025 report to 24.8 MtCO2eq in the 2026 report, and the 2030 target value moved from 8.9 MtCO2eq to 7.5 MtCO2eq), although the target reduction percentage remains at -70%.

socgen.resumen: Early achievement of the 2030 intensity target
socgen.descripcion: The emissions-intensity indicator recorded a sharp fall, moving from 114 gCO2/kWh in Q2 2024 to 85 gCO2/kWh in Q3 2025, comfortably beating the 2030 target of 125 gCO2/kWh well ahead of schedule.

socgen.resumen: Setback in the portfolio's alignment level
socgen.descripcion: The portfolio's alignment score worsened significantly, moving from -0.61 in Q2 2024 (aligned) to +0.16 in Q3 2025 (not aligned), moving away from the 0 target for 2030 due to a less favourable European context for green-steel projects.
The 51% emissions-intensity reduction target for 2030 versus 2021 is maintained, with no methodological changes or sharp deviations in progress.
No methodological changes or significant changes are reported in the emissions-intensity reduction targets (-20% for 2030 versus 2022) between the two reports.
The emissions-intensity reduction target remains at 18% for 2030 versus 2019, with normal progress in the indicator, which reached a 14% reduction in Q3 2025.

socgen.resumen: Apparent increase in intensity due to a change of data provider
socgen.descripcion: The portfolio's reported emissions intensity rose from 6.9 tCO2/t in Q2 2024 to 7.6 tCO2/t in Q3 2025, an increase the bank mainly attributes to a change of data provider aimed at improving data quality.

socgen.resumen: Early achievement of the 2030 alignment target
socgen.descripcion: The alignment score (Poseidon Principles) improved drastically, moving from +16.7% in 2023 to +7.9% at the end of 2024, comfortably beating the +15% target set for 2030 well ahead of schedule.
The target of reducing carbon-emissions intensity by 63% for 2030 versus 2022 levels is confirmed, with no methodological changes or reports of sharp changes.
The bank does not report specific decarbonization targets or metrics for this sector in either of the two reports analyzed.

socgen.resumen: Tightening of the sectoral policy and clarification of exemptions
socgen.descripcion: In March 2025, the thermal-coal sectoral policy was amended to broaden the definition of "coal developers," tighten exclusion thresholds for power producers with no phase-out commitments, and clarify the exemptions granted to energy-transition operations.
The anti-deforestation policies implemented in October 2024 were already reflected in the 2024 report, with no new variations or quantitative decarbonization targets reported in the 2025 report.

deutsche.resumen: Reduction in absolute financed emissions and impact from the exclusion of contingent commitments.
deutsche.descripcion: Scope 3 financed emissions fell from the 19.2 MtCO2/y reported for 2024 in the 2024 report to 17.6 MtCO2/y in the 2025 report, a reduction mainly explained by active portfolio management and by the exclusion of contingent-emission commitments from scope, which reduced the restated 2024 figure by 1.6 MtCO2/y.

deutsche.resumen: Downward recalibration of the base year, 2030 targets and intensities due to methodological improvements.
deutsche.descripcion: Sector emissions intensity fell notably from the 312 kgCO2e/MWh reported for year-end 2024 in the 2024 report to 195 kgCO2e/MWh in the 2025 report, after applying a methodological recalibration of the 2021 base year from 396 kgCO2e/MWh to 367 kgCO2e/MWh and of the 2030 target from 124 kgCO2e/MWh to 114 kgCO2e/MWh due to the exclusion of contingent commitments and more precise capture of smaller entities.

The steel portfolio's physical emissions intensity remained practically unchanged, moving from 1.234 kgCO2e/t of steel in the 2024 report to 1.231 kgCO2e/t of steel in the 2025 report, confirming the absence of material changes in the sector's performance.

deutsche.resumen: Continued progress in reducing manufacturers' physical emissions intensity.
deutsche.descripcion: Scope 3 emissions intensity for the light-vehicle segment fell from the 162 gCO2/vkm reported for 2024 in the 2024 report to 153 gCO2/vkm in the 2025 report, consolidating a 20% improvement versus the 190 gCO2/vkm baseline due to progress in clients' transition and the bank's active management.

deutsche.resumen: Recalibration of the base year and targets, while remaining above the decarbonization trajectory.
deutsche.descripcion: Although physical intensity fell from the 781 kgCO2e/t recorded for 2024 in the 2024 report to 749 kgCO2e/t in the 2025 report thanks to a low-intensity client, the portfolio remains 11% above the 2022 base year (recalibrated downward from 731 kgCO2e/t to 678 kgCO2e/t along with the 2030 target from 520 kgCO2e/t to 483 kgCO2e/t due to the exclusion of contingent commitments), evidencing the decarbonization challenges of this sector.

deutsche.resumen: Gradual reduction in the climate-alignment score under the Pegasus methodology.
deutsche.descripcion: The commercial-aviation portfolio's alignment indicator improved slightly, falling from 1.3% reported in the 2024 report to 1.0% in the 2025 report, representing a year-on-year reduction of 0.3 percentage points in the intensity of the commercial airlines operated.

deutsche.resumen: Strong improvement in alignment scores and update to the Poseidon Principles' Technical Guidance 5.2.
deutsche.descripcion: The climate-alignment score for the "Striving" scenario showed a notable reduction from the 19.7% reported for 2023 in the 2024 report to 7.5% reported for 2024 in the 2025 report, an improvement of 12.2 percentage points partly driven by the methodological update from Poseidon Principles Technical Guidance 5.1 to 5.2.

Total credit exposure to Commercial Real Estate secured by non-residential properties fell from EUR 69.1 billion in the 2024 report to EUR 61.9 billion in the 2025 report, remaining monitored under overall financed emissions but with no specific, independent decarbonization targets set.

deutsche.resumen: Reduction in financed emissions and energy intensity supported by model refinements.
deutsche.descripcion: Financed emissions for the European residential portfolio fell from 2.2 MtCO2e/y in the 2024 report to 2.0 MtCO2e/y in the 2025 report, with average intensity falling from 13.04 kgCO2e/m²/y to 12.5 kgCO2e/m²/y due to portfolio amortization and reduction together with refinements implemented in the CO2 estimation model.

deutsche.resumen: Increase in absolute financed emissions due to short-term lending activity.
deutsche.descripcion: Absolute Scope 3 financed emissions in the coal-mining sector rose from 4.6 MtCO2/y reported for 2024 in the 2024 report to 5.3 MtCO2/y in the 2025 report, a 16% increase mainly driven by short-term lending activity to a single client.
The aluminium sector is not within the scope of the institution's decarbonization-target framework or specific sectoral metrics in either of the two years analyzed.

deutsche.resumen: Monitored exclusively under the general ESG due-diligence framework with no quantitative targets.
deutsche.descripcion: The sector has no quantitative decarbonization targets, and its management is reflected in the number of transaction and client reviews initiated under agricultural-commodity and forestry guidelines, which fell from 244 in the 2024 report to 144 in the 2025 report due to procedural optimizations.

unicredit.resumen: Recalculation of the absolute baseline due to the inclusion of bonds and a readjustment of emissions scope.
unicredit.descripcion: Absolute financed emissions assigned to the 2021 baseline were recalculated downward, falling from the 21.4 MtCO2e detailed in the 2024 report to 19.4 MtCO2e in the 2025 report due to the inclusion of securities (bonds) and the readjustment of scope to strictly focus on integrated companies, refineries and the upstream segment.

unicredit.resumen: Methodological change to the metric due to the inclusion of corporate bond securities.
unicredit.descripcion: The bank recalculated its physical emissions-intensity baseline for 2021, moving from the 208 gCO2e/kWh reported in the 2024 report to 209 gCO2e/kWh in the 2025 report.

The sector shows absolute continuity in its strategic design, keeping its 2022 baseline unchanged at 1.45 tCO2/tSteel and its 2030 reduction target at 1.11 tCO2/tSteel in both the 2024 and 2025 reports.

Emissions-intensity metrics for this sector remained stable with no design-parameter changes, confirming a 2021 baseline of 161 gCO2/vkm and a set target of 95 gCO2/vkm in both the 2024 and 2025 reports.
The sector remains categorized under the exclusion criterion for lack of materiality, representing less than 1% of total exposure to carbon-intensive sectors in both the 2024 and 2025 reports.

This activity remains excluded from interim target-setting as its financial exposure sits below the EUR 1,000 million materiality threshold in the 2024 report and is confirmed under the same condition in the 2025 report.
Portfolio monitoring and the 30% reduction target set for 2030 remained constant versus the original 2022-baseline parameters in both the 2024 and 2025 reports.

unicredit.resumen: Introduction of mandatory collection of actual energy-performance certificates.
unicredit.descripcion: The bank strengthened its portfolio data management by establishing mandatory collection of actual Energy Performance Certificates (EPC) for new-business transactions in the 2025 report, going beyond the 2024 report's scheme (p. 245, 263), where only voluntary collection was encouraged or indirect estimates were used.

unicredit.resumen: Mandatory collection of actual energy certificates for new lending transactions.
unicredit.descripcion: The institution raised its data standards by implementing mandatory collection of Energy Performance Certificates (EPC) for new business in the 2025 report, improving control over data quality versus the 2024 report, which relied heavily on proxy-based methodologies and external estimates.
The progressive-divestment policy and the target of fully exiting thermal-coal-sector financing remain firmly set for 2028 in both the 2024 and 2025 reports.

The institution has not set specific targets for this segment due to its low relevance and materiality within the credit portfolio in the 2024 report, maintaining the same position and justification in the 2025 report.

unicredit.resumen: Formal planning for the development of guidelines, specific training and its own sectoral policies.
unicredit.descripcion: The bank expanded its level of commitment by announcing a future evaluation to establish internal guidelines on agricultural practices, an employee training track for 2026, and the formalization of a sector-specific policy in the 2025 report, going beyond the mere passive-monitoring stage recorded in the 2024 report.

intesa.resumen: The bank updated its benchmark to the IEA Dataset 2025 and reduced its exposure and financed emissions through portfolio management.
intesa.descripcion: The bank has updated its benchmark from the 2021 IEA Net Zero by 2050 Scenario to the 2025 IEA Dataset version. Drawn exposure fell from EUR 3,600 million to EUR 3,100 million, which contributed to a reduction in absolute financed emissions from 12.6 Mt CO2e to 10.9 Mt CO2e, supported by effective portfolio-management actions.

intesa.resumen: Update of the IEA Net Zero Scenario Benchmark from the 2023 version to the 2025 version.
intesa.descripcion: The bank has replaced the 2023 IEA Net Zero Scenario Benchmark with the updated 2025 IEA Net Zero Scenario Benchmark.

intesa.resumen: The bank updated its IEA baseline scenario to the 2025 version, implemented a new dedicated-financing approach for the iron and steel sector, and recorded an increase in its physical emissions intensity.
intesa.descripcion:
The bank updated its baseline scenario from the 2024 IEA Dataset to the 2025 version, which presents a less ambitious trajectory reflecting slower technology deployment in the sector.
In 2025, the bank introduced a new dedicated-financing approach for the iron and steel sector, accounting for these specific transactions differently versus general corporate lending.
Physical intensity rose from 0.82 tCO2/t of steel in 2024 to 0.90 tCO2/t in 2025 due to the inherent volatility of a hard-to-abate industry.

intesa.resumen: Update of the assessment scenario to the IEA Dataset 2025 and an increase in drawn exposure, resulting in a rise in absolute financed emissions from 1.0 to 1.1 Mt CO2e.
intesa.descripcion: The assessment scenario was updated from the 2024 IEA Dataset version to the 2025 IEA Dataset version. Drawn exposure rose from EUR 1,300 million to EUR 1,800 million, which raised absolute financed emissions from 1.0 Mt CO2e to 1.1 Mt CO2e.

intesa.resumen: Update of the benchmark to the IEA Dataset 2025 and a 50% reduction in absolute emissions due to fluctuations in exposure to counterparties.
intesa.descripcion: The benchmark used has been updated from the 2023 IEA Net Zero version to the 2025 IEA Dataset. Absolute emissions were cut in half, moving from 0.6 Mt CO2e to 0.3 Mt CO2e due to fluctuations in drawn exposure among counterparties.

intesa.resumen: The bank completed its exit from the coal sector in 2025, reducing its absolute emissions to zero and keeping only a minimal residual exposure.
intesa.descripcion: The bank confirmed reaching in 2025 its target of eliminating ("phase-out") exposures to the coal sector, reducing its absolute emissions from 0.1 Mt CO2e in 2024 to 0.0 Mt CO2e in 2025, keeping only a marginal amount of EUR 10 million attributable to a doubtful exposure.

intesa.resumen: A significant reduction was recorded in physical intensity and absolute CO2e emissions, driven by lower financial exposure in the sector.
intesa.descripcion: Physical intensity fell sharply from 4.38 tCO2e/t in 2024 to 3.03 tCO2e/t in 2025, while absolute emissions moved from 0.4 to 0.1 Mt CO2e, driven by a notable halving of the sector's financial exposure.

intesa.resumen: An increase was recorded in the agriculture sector's absolute emissions, which rose from 0.7 to 0.9 Mt CO2e.
intesa.descripcion: Absolute agriculture emissions rose, moving from 0.7 to 0.9 Mt CO2e.

intesa.resumen: ISP adjusted its reference scenario to an approach based on its portfolio composition and recorded a reduction in financed emissions from 2.0 to 1.8 Mt CO2e.
intesa.descripcion:
The reference scenario moved from using the standard "CRREM v2 1.5°C reduction pathway for Italy (2024)" model in 2024 to a more tailored approach called "CRREM 1.5°C reduction pathway for Italy adjusted on ISP's portfolio composition (v2 2024)" in 2025.
Absolute financed emissions fell from 2.0 Mt CO2e in 2024 to 1.8 Mt CO2e in 2025, driven by a higher proportion of properties with higher energy-performance ratings.

intesa.resumen: No relevant changes were identified in the reported period.

nordea.resumen: The sector recorded a 99.6% reduction in emissions due to portfolio restructuring and the ending of business relationships in Europe.
nordea.descripcion: The sector's actual absolute emissions fell sharply from 0.7 MtCO2e to 0.01 MtCO2e, a drastic 99.6% reduction versus the base year due to portfolio restructuring and the exit from business relationships with several European clients.

nordea.resumen: Reduction in Scope 1 and 2 absolute emissions despite growth in the credit portfolio.
nordea.descripcion: Scope 1 and 2 absolute emissions fell significantly, from 797,501 tCO2e to 361,603 tCO2e, even though the credit-portfolio volume grew from EUR 2,170 million to EUR 2,429 million.

nordea.resumen: No information is available in the reports consulted.
The bank revised its 2022 base-year emissions intensity upwards due to methodological and data-quality improvements.
nordea.descripcion: The bank has recalculated the 2022 base-year emissions intensity, moving from 113 gCO2e/km to 114 gCO2e/km due to a methodological evolution and improvements in data quality.

nordea.resumen: The information is not recorded in either of the reports consulted.
No information is available across the entire set of reports.
Indicates the information has not been included in the available reports.
Reduction in sectoral emissions intensity while maintaining the 30% reduction target for 2030.
nordea.descripcion: The sector's actual emissions intensity has fallen from 7.4 gCO2/dwt-nm to 7.0 gCO2/dwt-nm, keeping its 30% reduction target for 2030 unchanged.

nordea.resumen: The significant reduction in reported emissions intensity and volume is due to methodological improvements in energy-efficiency data quality.
nordea.descripcion: Reported emissions intensity fell by more than half, from 28 kgCO2e/m2 to 13 kgCO2e/m2, and absolute emissions fell from 420,212 tCO2e to 199,444 tCO2e, even though portfolio exposure increased. This inconsistency is explained by methodological improvements in the quality of Energy Performance Certificate (EPC) data.

nordea.resumen: The 2019 baseline was adjusted downward due to improvements in data quality and the use of new energy-efficiency labels.
nordea.descripcion: A significant adjustment has been made to the 2019 baseline, whose intensity fell from 17.4 kgCO2e/m2 to 12.2 kgCO2e/m2 due to large-scale updates in data quality and the use of new Energy Performance Certificate (EPC) label information.

nordea.resumen: No relevant changes were reported in the period.
The 2021 base-year intensity data were recalculated, turning the previously reported reduction into a 1.4% year-on-year increase versus the adjusted value.
nordea.descripcion: The 2021 base-year intensity underwent a drastic recalculation, falling from 758 tCO2e/EURm to 363 tCO2e/EURm. This change has caused the current actual-intensity figure (368 tCO2e/EURm) to now show a 1.4% year-on-year increase versus the adjusted base year, instead of the previously reported reduction.
